learning_objective: 🎯 Decode a modern political fable! Understand how Kolatkar uses the story of a shepherd, his dog, and starving tigers to satirize political corruption, fake treaties, and hypocrisy.

key_vocabulary.hindi_meaning: भेड़ों की रखवाली करने वाला कुत्ता

main_concepts.simple_explanation: The story begins with a tiger population that is starving. They complain to the Tiger King that Ajamil (the shepherd) has a fierce new sheepdog that protects his sheep so well that the tigers can't hunt.

The Tiger King boasts that he will defeat the dog. However, when he attacks, the sheepdog easily defeats the Tiger King, catching him in a humiliating grip. The dog represents the true, powerful defense force.

Instead of letting his dog finish off the threat, Ajamil (the politician/leader) steps in. He offers the embarrassed Tiger King a face-saving 'truce'. He signs a pact with the predators instead of destroying them.

The poem ends with Ajamil and the Tiger King pretending to be great friends, drinking together. The loyal sheepdog is ignored. The peace is a lie; it's a corrupt deal made between two powerful leaders who pretend to care about their subjects.

fun_activity.title: 📰 The Political Cartoon
fun_activity.instructions: This poem is a political allegory. If a newspaper were to draw a cartoon of this poem, who would the characters represent in the real world? The Shepherd = The Corrupt Politician. The Tigers = The Criminals/Enemies. The Sheepdog = The Army/Police. The Sheep = The innocent public!

exam_tips: 📌 An allegory is a story where characters represent larger concepts. You MUST explain that this poem is a satire on corrupt political alliances.
📌 The 'Truce' is highly ironic. A shepherd and a tiger cannot be friends. It shows that political leaders will make deals with criminals just to maintain a facade of peace.
📌 Contrast the honesty and capability of the Sheepdog with the cunning hypocrisy of Ajamil.
quick_recap: ⭐ A 'fable' is a short story, typically with animals as characters, conveying a moral. But Kolatkar twists the traditional fable to show a dark, cynical moral.
⭐ The Tiger King is shown as incompetent but full of false pride.
⭐ The poem exposes how the powerful (Ajamil and the King) manipulate situations for their own comfort, betraying those who actually do the hard work (the dog).
